candidates.original_title: Music, Pandas, and Muggers: On the Affective Psychology of Value
candidates.description: Study 4 tested whether affect-poor (no-empathy) conditions yield scope-sensitive responses and affect-rich (empathy) conditions yield scope-insensitive responses in recommended prison sentence for a mugger.
candidates.citation_sentence: we replicated Studies 2, 3 and 4 from Hsee and Rottenstreich (2004) replication and extension.
candidates.notes: No significant Scope x Empathy interaction was found (F(1,1006) = 1.06, p = 0.30, η² = 0.00). Authors state 'We found no support for a link between emotion and subjective value.' The main effects of scope and empathy were also not significant. No significant Scope x Empathy interaction (p = .30) and no significant main effects (all p's > .05). Authors state 'We found no support for a link between emotion and subjective value.' Pre-registered replication with simulated data placeholder noted in paper.

candidates.original_title: Music, Pandas, and Muggers: On the Affective Psychology of Value
candidates.description: Study 2 tested whether affect-poor (cash) targets yield scope-sensitive responses and affect-rich (music book) targets yield scope-insensitive responses in willingness to work at a campus bookstore.
candidates.citation_sentence: we replicated Studies 2, 3 and 4 from Hsee and Rottenstreich (2004) replication and extension.
candidates.notes: Authors explicitly state 'We failed to find support for replication hypotheses 1a and 1b.' All effects were null (all p's > .05). Pre-registered replication with simulated data placeholder noted in paper. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Music, Pandas, and Muggers: On the Affective Psychology of Value
candidates.description: In Study 4, sentencing judgments were expected to be scope-sensitive when participants received no empathy instruction and relatively scope-insensitive when participants received an empathy instruction.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a pre-registered experiment with an American online Amazon Mechanical Turk sample (N = 1010), we replicated Studies 2, 3 and 4 from Hsee and Rottenstreich (2004) replication and extension.
candidates.notes: The abstract reports no significant interaction for the Sentencing a Mugger replication, and the paper states that there was no support for the corresponding replication hypothesis. The results section is incomplete in places and the discussion is a placeholder, but no evidence supports success.

candidates.original_title: Music, Pandas, and Muggers: On the Affective Psychology of Value
candidates.description: In Study 2, cash as an affect-poor target was expected to produce scope-sensitive willingness to work, whereas a music book as an affect-rich target was expected to produce scope-insensitive willingness to work.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a pre-registered experiment with an American online Amazon Mechanical Turk sample (N = 1010), we replicated Studies 2, 3 and 4 from Hsee and Rottenstreich (2004) replication and extension.
candidates.notes: The replication authors explicitly state that they failed to find support for replication hypotheses 1a and 1b and found no significant Scope × Target interaction. The paper is a preregistration-stage draft with a placeholder discussion, but the reported results clearly indicate failure. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
